halt_reason: Still halted, but the scope has narrowed since round 1's entry. Measured 23 Nov and recorded route by route in docs/v2/build/probe/B05-environment-measurements.md: a Claude Code session on the founder's Mac can reach EVERY GitHub route this build needs - the full lock take/renew/release cycle works there, GraphQL works, /collaborators and /actions/permissions read back - while a cloud session can reach none of them. The refusals are therefore a cloud-session restriction, not a platform one. That unblocks Deliver 1-4 (identity, repository settings, both rulesets, and all twelve attacks including A4, A5, A6 and A12) provided they run from the Mac. It does NOT unblock Deliver 5-6: the three probes run through a CLOUD scheduled task, cloud was re-measured on 23 Nov and is unchanged, so B97 cannot run unattended and lock.py's release() still reports success on a lock it has not released. Two things must be settled before the founder spends the 45 minutes of clicking, because both change what gets built. First, whether unattended operation is still the goal: if it is, lock.py needs a backend that works from cloud, and that file is founder-owned and outside B05's touches, so it is its own small build and B05 waits; if it is not, the spec's option (a) puts one required approval on v2-build, which changes Deliver 3's ruleset and inverts A10's known answer from 'merges' to 'refused'. Second, which credential a Mac session uses: it reported login=vedantgautam1, but today that is both the founder's own gh keychain and the account Claude's GitHub connection uses, so the two are indistinguishable until the switch - and an attack run under the founder's own token proves nothing about the automation. One re-run of measure-env.sh after the identity switch settles the second question; only the founder can settle the first.
halt_options: RESOLVED since round 1: option 0 is answered. The Mac is not proxied - every route allowed, full lock cycle works. The founder also deleted lock/proxytest, and measure-env.sh deleted doc/b05-deltest. No stray branches remain.

THE DECISION, and it gates the 45 minutes of ruleset clicking: is an unattended loop still the goal? (i) Yes - then lock.py needs a release that does not depend on a route cloud sessions cannot reach, and GitHubRefs.delete must stop discarding its return code. Both files are founder-owned and outside B05's touches, so this is its own small spec the founder approves, and B05 resumes after it with v2-build's ruleset at zero approvals as written. (ii) No - then the spec's option (a) applies: one required approval on v2-build as well as main, the founder merges every build himself, Deliver 3's v2-build ruleset is built differently and A10's known answer inverts. (iii) Not yet - run Deliver 1-4 from the Mac now and leave 5-6 pending; this is worth having under both (i) and (ii), but it means building v2-build's ruleset at zero approvals and rebuilding it if the answer later turns out to be (ii).

WHAT TO DO FIRST, under any of (i)/(ii)/(iii), because it is needed by all three and answers the credential question: Deliver 2's identity work - create the automation account, add it as a collaborator, switch Claude's GitHub connection to it - then re-run measure-env.sh once on the Mac and once in cloud. That shows which account each session acts as and which credential supplies it (the script prints gh api user, gh auth status, and whether GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN are set, by length only, never the value). If a Mac session turns out to follow the founder's own gh keychain rather than Claude's connection, the attacks cannot be run from the Mac as the automation without giving that session the automation's own token, and that is a further fork for the founder rather than something this build decides.

KNOWN SIDE EFFECT, no action available: a success commit status named __b05probe__ sits permanently on v2-build's tip b9c4f5d, written by the first version of measure-env.sh before its A4 probe was pointed at a fake sha. GitHub does not allow statuses to be deleted. It does not weaken A4 (merges evaluate the head commit; it was posted by the founder's account, not the automation's) but it WILL appear in GitHub's required-status-checks picker while Deliver 3's rulesets are being built, and it must not be selected - nothing ever posts it, so requiring it would block every pull request.

STILL OPEN, for whoever writes the lock's correction: a cloud session can create and force-push a ref via git push but cannot delete one by any route, so a cloud-workable release cannot be a delete. Force-push to a released marker is one shape; a lock held as a file on a branch is another. B05 must not pick one - lock.py is outside its touches and designing its replacement here would be the spec widened by the back door.
